title: Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav Huna
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a distinguished student of Abaye and Rava, as in [Berakhot 34b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.34b.4), where he said, “I saw Abaye and Rava leaning sideways [in prayer]” (in [Megillah 22b–23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.22b.19-23a.1) Hyman considers the bar Avin reading erroneous); likewise [Yoma 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.53b.5), where he said, “I saw Abaye and Rava take three steps in a single bow”; and in [Niddah 40a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.40a.19) he spoke in Rava’s name. In [Keritot 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.25a.21-25b.1), “Rabbi Chiyya recited a baraita before Rava”; Hyman suggests that perhaps it should read “son of Rav Huna.” Likewise in [Ketubot 35b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.35b.2), “Rav Chiyya said to Rava,” Hyman suggests that perhaps it should read Rav Chiyya son of Rav Huna; and in [Berakhot 34b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.34b.14-16), where Rav Chiyya quotes Rav Safra, Hyman suggests that this may be Rav Chiyya son of Rav Huna.[^3] He is mentioned in [Shabbat 5a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.5a.18), resolving Rabbi Zeira’s words: “for example, where he caught it from on top of the wall.”

In [Pesachim 44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.44b.15) he said: “The Torah forbade only [flavor from] a pot used that day”; in [Avodah Zarah 67b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.67b.7) Hyman regards as corrupt the reading Rav Huna bar Chiyya.

In [Yevamot 119b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.119b.9): after Rav Papa’s answer, Rav Chiyya son of Rav Huna gives another case: when she says, “He and I hid in a cave.” There, at [81b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.81b.6), he resolves [it] as dissolved. In [Menachot 42b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.42b.2) he sent in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: “On the hand-tefillin one says … ‘to put on tefillin,’” etc.; Dikdukei Soferim cites the reading Rav Acha bar Huna, and Hyman prefers this reading.

notes.text: The heading fully writes Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav Huna; body Rav forms and the proposed bar Avin/Huna bar Chiyya/Acha alternatives remain distinct. The pot statement concerns its absorbed flavor rather than prohibiting the vessel as food. All identifications and preferred corrections remain Hyman’s, and taught-before-Rava is the reciter role.

Berakhot 34b directly names Chiyya son of Huna observing Abaye and Rava leaning. The other proposed bar Avin, Huna bar Chiyya and Acha substitutions remain occurrence-specific Hyman judgments; the exact Dikdukei Soferim reading was not inspected. The pot statement concerns absorbed flavor, and reciting before Rava is a role rather than a new tannaitic-era assignment.

[Berakhot 34b:14–16](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.34b.14-16) has the same ruling in two settings, with Rav or Rabbi Chiyya transmitting from Rav Safra in the name of an unnamed member of Rabbi’s household. Neither version supplies the patronymic that Hyman proposes. The parallel pot ruling in [Avodah Zarah 67b:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.67b.7) reverses the names and gives Rav Huna son of Rav Chiyya. Hyman gives Megillah 22a. The parallel begins at the end of 22b and reads Rav Chiyya bar Avin.
